LESSON: GRAMMAR IN USE 8.3.1 SENTENCES

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences

SECTION 1: WELCOME

• Today’s class: Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences
• How we learn: Teach → Worked example → Try this
• Use point notes. Show working. Then take the quiz.
• Big question: What are some of your school rules?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

1. identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text
2. use question tags and double imperatives correctly in sentences

SECTION 3: CLASS STUDY (TEACH → EXAMPLE → TRY)

▸ Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences

• Listen to a model.
• Study the example.
• Then produce your own example.

▸ Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences

Teach
• Focus skill: identify questions tags and double imperatives from a text.
• Use complete sentences.
• Speak clearly; write neatly.

Worked example
• Model sentence 1 about Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences.
• Model sentence 2 using a Kenyan school example.
• Model dialogue: A: “…?”  B: “…”

Try this
• Write 5 original sentences on this skill.
• Say one 30-second oral example to a partner.


SECTION: QUICK EXAMPLES

• One clear model for Grammar in Use 8.3.1 Sentences
• One Kenyan school/home example

SECTION: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences.
2. Do one oral practice with a partner.
3. Correct spelling/punctuation.

SECTION: WORK TO DO

1. Revision sheet: meaning + 5 examples + 5 practice items.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. What are some of your school rules?
2. How do you give instructions?
3. Why do we ask questions?

SECTION: REMEMBER

• Model first, then try.
• Use complete sentences.

• Next: complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Classroom study notes (Strategy 2)
